title: See-No-Evil Monkey Emoji 🙈 Meaning: Shy or Cringing
description: The 🙈 see-no-evil monkey covers its eyes. In texts it means embarrassed, shy, or 'I can't look.' Learn its flirty use, examples and proverb origins.
summary: The 🙈 see-no-evil monkey emoji shows a monkey covering its eyes. In messages it rarely has anything to do with evil. It means embarrassment, shyness, or not being able to watch: a bashful reaction after a confession, a compliment, a mistake, or something cringeworthy.
meaning: Hiding your face is what people do when they are embarrassed, and 🙈 turns that gesture into an emoji. It is the most used of the three monkeys by a wide margin. Someone sends it after admitting a crush, sharing a photo they are unsure about, making a typo in the work chat, or saying something a bit too honest. The monkey softens the moment, as if peeking through its fingers to see how you will react.

It is a staple of flirting for the same reason. A bold message followed by 🙈 says 'I can't believe I just sent that,' which lets the sender be forward while appearing shy. Replying to a compliment with it signals pleased bashfulness. The other common use is secondhand embarrassment: watching someone else's awkward moment, a trailer that looks dreadful, or your own old posts, and not being able to look.

The source is the proverb 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil,' pictured as three monkeys. The best-known version is a seventeenth-century carving at the Toshogu shrine in Nikko, Japan, where this monkey is called Mizaru. Occasionally the emoji is used in that original sense, for choosing to ignore wrongdoing or pretending not to notice something, but that is far less common than simple shyness.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: This is one of the clearer flirting tells. People add 🙈 after saying something vulnerable, like 'I was hoping you'd text.' It expresses nervous interest and invites a kind reply. If someone sends it after you compliment them, they are flattered and a little flustered.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use it for confessions and blunders: 'I forgot your birthday 🙈.' It works as a light apology by showing the sender is cringing at themselves. It also answers awkward stories, standing in for 'oh no, I can't watch.' The tone stays warm and self-aware.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Captions on unpolished selfies, throwback photos, and first attempts at something use 🙈 to pre-empt judgment. In comments it reacts to cringe content or spoilers the viewer wants to avoid. It appears on posts about scary movies too, as a literal 'covering my eyes.'

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: In casual team chat it can accompany a minor slip, such as sending a message to the wrong channel. It is friendly but cutesy, so use it with peers and not in formal apologies or with clients, where it may look like you are not taking an error seriously.

combos.meaning: The full proverb: see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil, or staying out of drama.
Shy affection, typical of early flirting.

confusedWith.difference: 🫣 covers its face but peeks with one eye, so it stresses morbid curiosity and nervous fascination. 🙈 has both eyes fully hidden and is more about bashfulness and embarrassment, with a cuter feel.
🙊 covers its mouth and means 'oops, I shouldn't have said that' or 'my lips are sealed.' 🙈 covers its eyes and is about not wanting to look or be seen.
😳 shows wide eyes and red cheeks for being caught off guard or flustered. 🙈 is more playful and deliberate: the sender is hiding in a cute way, not frozen in shock.

avoid: Do not use it to brush off a serious mistake that hurt someone, where coyness looks like dodging responsibility.
Never use monkey emojis in reference to a person's race or ethnicity; that use is racist.
Avoid it in formal communication, since it reads as young and flirtatious.
design: The emoji shows a brown monkey's face from the front with both hands held over its eyes. Most vendors draw a round head with a lighter face and ears and a slight smile below the hands. Fur shades and hand positions vary a little, but all platforms keep the eyes completely covered.

faqs.q: What does 🙈 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is feeling shy, embarrassed, or flustered, often in a good way. After a compliment or a flirty line, it usually means she liked it. After a mistake, it is a sheepish 'oops.'

faqs.q: What does 🙈 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: The same thing: bashfulness or embarrassment. Guys often use it after saying something sweet or revealing, to take the edge off being vulnerable. It is commonly a sign he cares how you will react.

faqs.q: Where do the three monkey emojis come from?
faqs.a: They illustrate a Japanese pictorial proverb. The monkeys are named Mizaru, Kikazaru, and Iwazaru, covering eyes, ears, and mouth. Their names play on the Japanese word for monkey, and the most famous carving is at Nikko's Toshogu shrine.
Often. It is not flirtatious in every message, but it is strongly associated with playful shyness. Paired with a personal admission or a compliment, it is a common flirting signal.
It can, in line with the proverb, as in 'I'm pretending I didn't see that.' This use is the minority. Most of the time the monkey is hiding out of embarrassment.
